entries.proposition: Material scope: the compounds are mibefradil, NNC55-0396, ML218, nickel and nifedipine, in rat embryonic day 14 cortical progenitor cultures, 24 h exposure. Ethosuximide is not among them and no antiseizure drug used in children is tested.
entries.snippet: Primary NPCs were isolated from the cerebral cortex of Sprague-Dawley (SD) rat embryos (embryonic day 14 or E14)

entries.proposition: Viability: all T-type blockers except ML218 decreased progenitor viability; the L-type blocker nifedipine did not. The authors infer simultaneous Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 block is responsible.
entries.snippet: All of the T-type calcium channel blockers, except ML218, decreased NPC cellular viability.
entries.anchor: Results, T-type calcium channels are required for maintenance of NPC viability

entries.proposition: Specificity limit: differentiated astrocytes (no Cav3 expression) were not affected, and neurons were affected only by the broader blocker; the authors cannot assign subtype roles because subtype-selective blockers do not exist and say so.
entries.snippet: In our study, we could not explain the subtype-specific roles of T-type calcium channels due to lack of subtype-specific blockers for CaV3.1, 3.2 and 3.3.

entries.proposition: Mechanism: within 10 minutes the two blockers lowered phosphorylation of AKT (Ser473) and of GSK3 beta (Ser9) without changing ERK, JNK or p38. Ser9 phosphorylation inhibits GSK3 beta, so lower Ser9 phosphorylation corresponds to higher GSK3 beta activity; the paper does not measure GSK3 beta activity, and attributes cell death to the pathway as a possibility.
entries.snippet: Within 10 min of treatment, mibefradil and NNC55-0396 decreased AKT (Ser473) phosphorylation, without affecting ERK, JNK, or p38 signaling (Fig. 4C).
entries.anchor: Results, T-type calcium channel blockers rapidly decrease AKT phosphorylation

entries.proposition: The authors' safety statement and its limit: they say their findings point to a possible safety issue for T-type blockers, especially in pregnancy, and explicitly state that in-vivo effects were not specified.
entries.snippet: Although we could not specify the in vivo effects of T-type calcium channel blockers, future studies of T-type calcium channels in developmental disorders such as autism, will provide insight into the essential role of these channels in neural development.

entries.proposition: The authors note that mice lacking either Cav3.1 or Cav3.2 are not embryonic lethal, and read that as mutual compensation; single-gene null viability is therefore a counterpoint to the pharmacological toxicity signal.
entries.snippet: Indeed, either CaV3.1 or CaV3.2 knockout mice did not show embryo lethality (Kim et al., 2001; Harraz et al., 2015), suggesting that CaV3.1 and CaV3.2 can compensate for deficiency in another subunit.

entries.proposition: Developmental window: cortical Cav3.1 is high in the embryo, lower in the perinatal period and higher again from about postnatal day 11, by their blot. The blot (Figure 1C) is one lane per age with no quantification or n and the text describes the postnatal rise as smaller than the embryonic level.
entries.snippet: CaV3.1 expression was prominent during the prenatal period, transiently decreased during the perinatal period, and increased again by postnatal day 11, although this increase was to a lesser extent than that observed during the embryonic period.
entries.anchor: Results, CaV3.1 is the dominant subtype in neural progenitor cells

entries.proposition: Figure 4, page 5 render: pAKT over AKT falls to about 0.75 and 0.46 of control at two concentrations of NNC55-0396 and to about 0.57 and 0.35 at two of mibefradil; pGSK3 beta over GSK3 beta falls to about 0.65 and 0.5 (NNC) and about 0.67 and 0.33 (mibefradil), significance stars at the higher concentrations (N = 3 to 5). Panel C: pERK, pJNK, pP38 over total unchanged. These are in-vitro micromolar concentrations of research compounds, about the potency of those compounds on the channels and not the exposure of any clinical drug.

entries.proposition: Figure 2, page 3 render: NNC55-0396 viability steps from about 85 percent at 0.6 micromolar to about 50 percent at 1.2 and about 10 percent at 2.5; mibefradil to about 45 percent at 5 and about 30 at 10; ML218 stays near 100 to about 85 percent; nickel loses viability above 250 micromolar; nifedipine flat; astrocytes unaffected; neurons about 80 and 60 percent with mibefradil, not with NNC55-0396. A table in panel A assigns blocker-to-subtype mapping as the authors' reading.
